issues.problem: The new Stop release (R4-05) runs `exit 0` from stop-check.sh, so once it releases, everything after it is skipped: the L-04 stall block, HOOK-14 and the planning floor (required_planning). Any agent can trigger this on purpose by calling Stop 6 times while an orchestrator queue is pending. That queue exists for every composer run, and orchestrator.json does not change between Stops. The core planning-floor gate is then bypassed with no audit trail. Before this change, the orchestrator block trapped the session; now the agent gets out past the floor.
issues.evidence: Sandbox (HOME=REVF-G5-probe/home, runtime claude): project with dirty tree, state file holding only 'silver-feature'. Without orchestrator.json, Stop gives {decision:block,'missing required skills: silver-quality-gates, silver-context, silver-plan'}. With orchestrator.json {current_flow:FLOW-PLAN,repo_root:<proj>}, Stops 1-5 give 'Orchestrator parent: flow queue pending (FLOW-PLAN)...' and Stops 6 and 7 give empty output, rc 0, so the floor never runs. tests/hooks/test-stop-check-paths.sh:99-117 locks this in: it asserts an empty reason ('third Stop with no progress is released') on a reset_state fixture that is missing planning skills, the same fixture whose baseline at :66 blocks on the floor.
issues.suggested_fix: On release, skip only the orchestrator block and fall through to the remaining stop-check checks (wrap the two orchestrator blocks in `if ! sb_orchestrator_stop_block_released; then ... fi`, never exit 0). Log the release to the event log. Change the test: once released, a Stop with missing planning skills must still block on the floor, and only a Stop with the planning skills recorded may print nothing.

issues.problem: Worker identity now comes only from the payload's agent_id (Claude) or SB_ORCHESTRATOR_WORKER=1 in the hook process environment. Codex payloads carry no agent id, and nothing in the Codex adapter or installer sets the variable. In the default parent mode a Codex session therefore cannot edit at all: the parent is denied, and spawn_agent workers are denied too, because they are classified as the parent. The old marker made Codex work, insecurely. This change turns that into a full block of legitimate work on a primary host. The author raised it only as a question in the notes but marked R4-02 'fixed'.
issues.evidence: SILVER_BULLET_RUNTIME=codex, parent-mode project: PreToolUse apply_patch {command:'*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: src/a.txt ...'} with no agent id, the shape a Codex spawn_agent worker sends -> deny '🛑 ORCHESTRATOR PARENT — apply_patch is forbidden in parent mode'. `grep agent_id hooks/codex-hook-adapter.sh` finds nothing; only the external delegate scripts (scripts/agent-*/lib.sh) export SB_ORCHESTRATOR_WORKER.
issues.suggested_fix: Settle this before merge (needs-user/orchestrator decision): find out whether Codex subagent hook calls carry a distinct session or thread id and map it in the adapter, for example a per-spawn session-id map written by the parent spawn_agent PreToolUse and matched per call. If no Codex signal exists, make parent-mode enforcement advisory on Codex (tier < 2) and document it, rather than blocking every edit. Add a Codex-runtime test either way.

issues.problem: Sanctioned parent commands accept any NAME=value or env prefix without checking the variable. BASH_ENV=<existing file> makes the bash-based scripts/silver-bullet source that file, and PATH=<dir> picks a different silver-bullet, so the parent can run the contents of an existing script that no hook inspects. F2's read-only verdict refuses the same prefixes on read-only commands (LD_PRELOAD=, GIT_PAGER=), so G5 is weaker than F2 here. A 'bash <file>' wrapper whose script basename is silver-bullet (F2 reports opaque:true) is accepted as well.
issues.evidence: Guard results for the parent: 'BASH_ENV=src/a.txt silver-bullet invoke-skill silver' -> ALLOW; 'PATH=/tmp/evil silver-bullet invoke-skill silver' -> ALLOW; "env BASH_ENV=src/a.txt bash -c 'silver-bullet invoke-skill silver'" -> ALLOW; 'bash silver-bullet invoke-skill silver' -> ALLOW (F2 opaque_reasons: 'runs a shell script'); 'LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/x.so git status' -> deny.
issues.suggested_fix: Deny sanctioned commands that carry assignments or env options (or allow only a short safe list), and deny when F2 reports opaque for the 'bash <script>' form unless the script resolves to the plugin's own scripts/silver-bullet.

issues.problem: Only F2's write_paths and patch paths are checked. Tree-scope writes that F2 reports in .writes[] (scope 'tree': git reset --hard, git apply, git stash pop, git checkout .) and opaque writers are allowed during an active delegation. In parent mode the directive guard already denies these, so the remaining exposure is worker sessions racing a delegated external agent.
issues.evidence: Delegation {active:true,ownership_scope:[src]}, exec_command: 'git reset --hard' -> ALLOW, 'git apply p.diff' -> ALLOW, 'git stash pop' -> ALLOW, while F2 JSON for 'git reset --hard' has writes:[{path:<repo root>,via:'git reset',scope:'tree'}].
issues.suggested_fix: Treat a .writes[] entry with scope 'tree' whose path contains an ownership_scope entry as in scope.
